newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Aug 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Aug 6.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Supreme Court gives fresh hope to a pro-Ramos group by allowing to hear its petition that will lead to the lifting of the term limit of President Fidel Ramos. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- Petroleum companies deny charges that they colluded to raise their pump prices on August 1. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- Opposition leaders urged President Fidel Ramos to let Defense Secretary Renato de Villa resign. De Villa is running for president next year. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Senators say they will boycott their regular meeting with President Fidel Ramos due to an escalating feud over the anti-drug campaign. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Consumer prices rise by a lower-than-expected 4.8 percent in July, unchanged from the June inflation level, officials say. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- Bankers Association of the Philippines lifts its two percent ceiling on over-the-counter dollar selling rate. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- Exports rise by 18.5 percent to a record $2.126 billion in June, paced by increases in overseas sales of electronics and computer parts. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
